summary: A New Year gathering at one friend's house, and the top comment is a request for next year's episodes to run over an hour — this audience wants more footage, not tighter edits. A large emotional cluster is directed at Vee, who was going through something publicly difficult at the time: viewers tell her she did not deserve it, that she is still one of the best singers around, and that they are behind her, using the comment section as a support space rather than a review. Ammy gets her own appreciation thread, both as the funniest moment of the episode and as the one tomboy the commenters say they love, which reads as representation being valued. The channel's own pinned comment asks openly what the group should do next and where they should go, and viewers answer with crossover ideas.

audience_signals: The channel already runs live audience research — a pinned comment asking what the group should do next and where to go, answered with concrete crossover ideas
The demand here is for longer episodes, not shorter ones, which cuts against the general assumption that this audience wants everything compressed
Friendsfly is consumed as a monthly appointment; predictable cadence is part of the product
The comment section functions as a support space when a cast member is in public difficulty, which is a form of loyalty that no reach metric captures
A visibly queer cast member is named approvingly as the one the audience loves, so representation in the group is an asset rather than a risk
content_requests: A crossover with the ปล่อยกูไป format abroad
